title: Two EU AI Act translations use FLOPs/s instead of cumulative FLOPs
content:
ARXO-2026-0413 · Reported
AI Act, Portuguese and Croatian versions: the 10^25 threshold of Article 51(2) is measured per second
The other 22 versions measure the cumulative amount of computation in floating point operations, without a time unit. The added words do not fit the cumulative quantity described in the same paragraph. Recital 111 and Annex XIII, point (c), support a total number of operations.
Consequence
In a hypothetical case with a constant training rate, 2×10^25 operations over a million seconds means 2×10^19 operations per second. The total is above 10^25; the rate is not.
Proposed correction
Delete the words per second (por segundo, u sekundi) in Article 51(2).

Evidence
Reproduced by execution. Quotations are verbatim from the official material; translations are ours and marked.
medido em operações de vírgula flutuante por segundo
Our translation (English): measured in floating point operations per second
iskazana brojem matematičkih operacija nad brojevima s pomičnim zarezom u sekundi
Our translation (English): expressed as the number of floating point operations per second
the cumulative amount of computation used for its training measured in floating point operations is greater than

pt
Regulamento da Inteligência Artificial, versões portuguesa e croata: o limiar de 10^25 do artigo 51.º, n.º 2, é medido por segundo
As outras 22 versões medem a quantidade acumulada de cálculo em operações de vírgula flutuante, sem unidade de tempo. As palavras acrescentadas não correspondem à quantidade acumulada descrita no mesmo número. O considerando 111 e o anexo XIII, alínea c), apontam para um número total de operações.
Consequence
Num caso hipotético com uma taxa de treino constante, 2×10^25 operações ao longo de um milhão de segundos correspondem a 2×10^19 operações por segundo. O total é superior a 10^25; a taxa não é.
Proposed correction
Suprimir, no artigo 51.º, n.º 2, as palavras «por segundo» na versão portuguesa e «u sekundi» na versão croata.
hr
Akt o umjetnoj inteligenciji, portugalska i hrvatska verzija: prag od 10^25 iz članka 51. stavka 2. mjeri se u sekundi
Ostale 22 verzije mjere kumulativnu količinu računanja u matematičkim operacijama nad brojevima s pomičnim zarezom, bez jedinice vremena. Dodane riječi ne odgovaraju kumulativnoj količini opisanoj u istom stavku. Uvodna izjava 111. i Prilog XIII. točka (c) upućuju na ukupan broj operacija.
Consequence
U hipotetskom slučaju sa stalnom brzinom treniranja, 2×10^25 operacija tijekom milijun sekundi znači 2×10^19 operacija u sekundi. Ukupan broj veći je od 10^25; brzina nije.
Proposed correction
U članku 51. stavku 2. brisati riječi „por segundo” u portugalskoj verziji i „u sekundi” u hrvatskoj verziji.

report.summary: Portuguese and Croatian versions of the EU AI Act add 'per second' to the 10^25 FLOPs systemic-risk threshold, turning a cumulative test into a rate test.
report.background: Article 51(2) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 presumes that a general-purpose AI model poses systemic risk when the cumulative compute used for training, measured in floating point operations, exceeds 10^25 — a figure roughly in the range of GPT-4-class training runs and drawn from compute-scaling research. The rule became operational for general-purpose model providers in August 2025, and the Commission is drafting guidelines that will interpret it. EU regulations are equally authentic in all 24 official languages, so lawyer-linguists in the Council and Parliament produce parallel versions that are meant to be legally identical. Translation drift in a quantitative threshold is unusually consequential: numbers and units carry the legal test itself, not just its phrasing. ARXO, which maintains a register of legislative discrepancies, compared all 24 language versions and found two that diverge from the rest, then reported the issue to the Council, Parliament and the European AI Office.
key_points: The discrepancy is narrow but material: the Portuguese text says 'medido em operações de vírgula flutuante por segundo' and the Croatian says 'u sekundi' — 'per second' — while the other 22 language versions, including English, describe a cumulative total with no time unit.

Internal evidence favours the cumulative reading. Recital 111 and Annex XIII point (c) refer to a total number of operations, and the same paragraph of Article 51(2) explicitly frames the quantity as 'cumulative', so the added time unit contradicts its own sentence.

The practical effect is drastic. A model trained at 2×10^19 FLOP/s for a million seconds (~11.6 days) accumulates 2×10^25 operations — above the threshold — but its rate is nowhere near 10^25 per second. Under the mistranslated test, essentially no real training run would qualify.

ARXO's proposed fix is minimal: delete the two words 'por segundo' and 'u sekundi' from Article 51(2), which would require a corrigendum issued through the Council's and Parliament's lawyer-linguist procedures.

The finding was reproduced by direct comparison of the Official Journal files, with hashes recorded, and reported to the Council General Secretariat, Parliament's Directorate for Legislative Acts and the European AI Office on 31 October 2026; no response has been recorded.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the ambiguity matters most in the two affected languages: a provider reading the Portuguese or Croatian text could argue its model falls outside the systemic-risk presumption, triggering extra obligations around evaluation, adversarial testing, incident reporting and cybersecurity. Regulators and courts would likely resolve the conflict by reading Article 51(2) in light of the other 22 versions and Recital 111, but that requires litigation or guidance rather than being self-evident. Developers and compliance teams should model obligations on the cumulative 10^25 threshold regardless of language. More broadly, the case exposes how quantitative rules depend on translation quality, and it argues for systematic machine-assisted cross-language consistency checks before regulations take effect — and for corrigenda to be issued quickly when drift is found.
report.tools: To follow up: EUR-Lex (eur-lex.europa.eu) publishes all 24 language versions of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 for direct comparison; the European AI Office's pages and the AI Act Service Desk host guidance and the pending systemic-risk guidelines; Epoch AI's training-compute dataset helps estimate whether a model sits near 10^25 FLOPs; ARXO's Findings Register tracks this and similar discrepancies; and the open-source `eurlex` Python package plus public AI Act explorer sites make bulk cross-language text checks reproducible.
